messages:
Noah Kim: quick postmortem follow-up: tail spikes traced to continuous-batcher growing windows when many tiny requests arrive interleaved with large seq requests. proposal: introduce 'isolation buckets' that separate tiny interactive flows from bulk streams at the queueing layer.

Rina Gupta: isolation buckets = per-tenant (or per-route) soft lanes? main tradeoff is KV cache dilution and GPU slot fragmentation. how are we bounding state?

Noah Kim: soft lanes, not hard pins. allocate buckets lazily on detection and enforce global caps. buckets route requests to smaller micro-windows (10-40ms) with stricter max batch sizes. they can bleed back into main batcher if underutilized.

Diego Flores: eviction semantics? if buckets saturate, do we preempt buckets or main batches? preference: preempt buckets first to preserve throughput for heavy jobs.

Noah Kim: agreed. default is preempt buckets when global free slots < 8%. we also consider shedding tiny low-priority requests first.

Maya Lin: metrics we need: per-bucket p50/p95/p99, KV_hit_by_bucket, bucket_alloc_count, demotion_count, bucket_preempt_events. also an alert when demotion_rate > 2% in 5m.

Rina Gupta: operational exposure: prefer tiered defaults (free/standard/premium) controlling bucket sizes. avoid per-tenant knobs unless enterprise opt-in.

Diego Flores: what about fairness across noisy neighbors? add decay on bucket credit and a cooldown on repeated allocations. prevent refill gaming by enforcing min_interburst_gap.

Noah Kim: included those: credit_decay, cooldown_ms, min_interburst_gap_ms. rollout: stage small fleet 2% traffic, 48h A/B, watch KV hit and p99 interactive. tagging @maya for dashboards.

Ops-bot: checklist: schedule stage rollout? -> yes. create alerts: demotion_rate, per-bucket_KV_drop.

Maya Lin: will add dashboard and a replay hook. also request: record deterministic decision logs for debugging so we can replay allocation/demotion sequences.

Noah Kim: will add deterministic_seed and decision log. will report results after the A/B.
